_comment: PathTriage Primitive 03 — IAM modification (mutate) preventive SCP. Restricts CreatePolicyVersion and SetDefaultPolicyVersion to tag-authorized identities. Companion to the detection query in cloudtrail_lake_query.sql.

Statement._comment_on_this_statement: AWS-managed policies cannot actually be modified — this statement is defense-in-depth. AWS blocks these operations service-side, but the SCP makes the denial explicit and auditable.

_notes.coverage: First statement enforces tag-based authorization for policy mutation. Only principals tagged 'iam-policy-mgmt-authorized=true' or matching approved role name patterns can perform CreatePolicyVersion / SetDefaultPolicyVersion.
_notes.content_limitation: SCPs cannot inspect the policyDocument content of a CreatePolicyVersion call. An authorized policy manager can still inject wildcards into any customer-managed policy. This is the fundamental limitation of the preventive layer — content-level protection requires runtime detection (this primitive's SQL query) and manual review workflow.
_notes.asymmetry_with_azure: Azure enforces a service-side privilege-escalation guard on the equivalent action (D-Z4-02): a principal cannot inject actions they do not themselves hold, regardless of whether they are tag-authorized. AWS has no such guard. Documented in azure_symmetry.md as a structural asymmetry contributing to thesis Section 4.
_notes.cross_version_gap: Attackers can iteratively modify a policy across many version updates, each within their allowed action set, until the cumulative changes reach admin-equivalent. Detection primitive's baseline join captures this — each version's delta is scored — but SCP alone does not.
_notes.deployment: Attach at the organisation root. Requires all legitimate policy-management identities to be tagged 'iam-policy-mgmt-authorized=true' before deployment. Combine with a separate policy review workflow (out of PathTriage scope) for the content-level check.
